original_test_intent: Subject the platform to the project-defined WR recovery cycle and verify every required PCIe endpoint and link returns at the approved generation and width after each cycle without boot, AER, device or service-health regression.
original_method: Select the unique row; obtain the authoritative WR definition and exact reboot mechanism; map all target endpoints/root ports/switches/retimers and baseline enumeration, LnkCap/LnkSta plus preserved logs; quiesce jobs and data; perform the approved count/timing of cycles; after each readiness checkpoint collect complete PCIe and platform-health evidence; abort on the first abnormal cycle and recover through the independent console.
manual_activity: An authorized operator confirms WR semantics, approves and initiates each disruptive cycle and owns recovery; the agent can collect post-readiness PCIe and health evidence.
required_inputs: Authoritative expansion and power-state semantics of WR
Approved reboot/reset control path, cycle count, interval, readiness deadline and final state
PCIe endpoint/slot/serial/BDF and root-port/switch/retimer generation-width matrix
Workload drain, data-protection, maintenance approval, error/thermal limits and console recovery plan
safety_requirements: Do not infer WR from adjacent DC/AC rows; use the project definition
Drain users/jobs and flush data before disruptive cycles
Preserve existing logs and correlate each cycle by timestamp
Authenticate the exact SUT and control path before any reboot/reset
Stop on boot timeout, missing device, link downgrade/retrain, AER/device fault, thermal/power anomaly or service instability; no automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate identity, WR definition, cycle plan, topology, approval and recovery readiness
Collect complete pre/post/per-cycle PCIe, boot, OS/BMC, error and telemetry evidence
Initiate only the explicitly approved named reboot/reset action after separate execution confirmation
Do not infer WR, clear logs, choose count/timing, continue after failure, retry automatically or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Define WR and approve its distinction from DC and AC cycling
Approve control method, count/timing, target link matrix, readiness/error oracle and recovery
Review per-cycle evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Repeated warm reboot is plausible but not proven by the literal acronym. The prose identifies no command or controller, and lspci evidence alone does not authorize a disruptive cycle.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After WR is authoritatively defined, use only the approved control path for the specified cycles and collect complete `lspci -Dnnvvv` plus correlated boot/BMC/host evidence after every readiness point.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The WR-cycle title, overnight/720-minute intent and speed/link criterion remain; semantics, count, timing and exact normal matrix are pending.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Execute a bounded, timestamped engineering-defined WR cycle matrix and preserve full per-cycle enumeration, link, readiness and error evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the undefined acronym and cycle plan explicit prerequisites instead of silently equating WR with warm reboot.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: DC, AC or a single reboot result cannot substitute until engineering defines the required WR state transition.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Different reset types preserve different PCIe switch/retimer/device states; using the wrong reboot primitive can appear healthy while never exercising the intended recovery path.

project_override_considerations: Engineering must distinguish WR from DC and AC cases by the exact hardware/software state retained across the transition. A warm OS reboot is only a candidate interpretation, not an approved assumption.
expected_evidence: Approved WR definition, control command/path, cycle schedule and operator authorization
Target endpoint/slot/BDF/root-port/switch/retimer matrix with baseline and every-cycle LnkCap/LnkSta
Every-cycle transition audit, boot/readiness time, enumeration and service health
Correlated AER/dmesg/journal/BMC/SEL plus thermal/power evidence without cleared history

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The code/row/variant is unique. The ambiguity is semantic: adjacent DC/AC rows do not authorize expanding WR as warm reboot.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The link-recovery cycle objective is identifiable, and the WR definition plus cycle/topology oracle are supplyable engineering inputs. Execution stays gated but static review can complete.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2210 Wistron-HW-00488-V003: define the authoritative meaning and state boundary of WR and its distinction from DC/AC, approve the exact reboot/reset control path, cycle count/interval/readiness deadline/final state, target endpoint/slot/serial/BDF/root-port/switch/retimer generation-width matrix, AER/retrain/error/thermal limits, workload drain, maintenance authorization, aborts and independent-console recovery.

review_improvement: Prevents an unapproved acronym expansion, retains the long-duration PCIe recovery intent and creates a complete per-cycle evidence and recovery contract.
independent_technical_reasoning: Reset primitives differ in whether endpoint power, PCIe switch state, firmware and link training are reinitialized. Therefore interpreting WR from neighboring rows would be a prohibited semantic guess and could leave the intended state boundary untested. Each cycle needs its own topology and link record because a final sample hides intermittent recovery faults. Workload quiescence and console recovery are mandatory because even a warm reboot disrupts the OS and may fail before remote access returns.
